The '''Belcanto Nations''', officially the '''Federal Republic of the Belcanto Nations''', is a federal parliamentary republic that emerged from Vesperan occupation after the [[Avant Great War]]. The state is often shortened in political and map labels to Belcanto or the Republic of Belcanto.

== Historical Background ==

Before Vesperan conquest, the Belcantese polities maintained independence through diplomacy, federal coordination, defensive geography, and a shared musical-cultural tradition. The old source describes the pre-imperial state as the [[United Kingdoms of Belcanto]], a federation or united kingdoms whose identity centered on the [[Belcantese Language|Belcantese]] phrase ''Belkanski'', meaning "white song" or "pure song."

The [[Belcanto Campaign]] of 1892-1895 ended Belcantese independence and brought the region under the [[Vesperan Empire]]. The occupation lasted until 1949.

== Vesperan Occupation ==

Vesperan rule dissolved older federal institutions, including the [[Council of Seven Crowns]], and replaced them with imperial administration. The occupation redirected local resources, ports, forests, mines, and skilled labor into the imperial economy. It also attempted to suppress Belcantese language and cultural practices in favor of Vesperan imperial identity through policies such as the [[Imperial Cultural Integration Decree of 1897]].

The occupation produced a durable underground culture. Traditional music, literature, and local political networks survived through clandestine groups later remembered collectively as the [[Belcantese Cultural Resistance]].

== Independence ==

The collapse of local Vesperan authority in Belcanto during the empire's final year allowed the [[Belcantese Independence Movement]] to form a provisional government. The [[Declaration of Belcantese Independence]] was proclaimed on 15 May 1949 in [[Belgrad]], before the formal end of the wider [[Avant Great War]] on 3 December 1949.

The new federal republic drew on older regional autonomy while creating national institutions capable of reconstruction. The [[Federal Constitution of 1949]] provided the basic postwar framework. Its early years were dominated by food supply, infrastructure repair, refugee return, language restoration, and the reintegration of territories damaged by war and occupation.

== Territorial Disputes ==

The 1951 settlement resolved many borders but left disputes with Khalindar over territory that Khalindar claimed had been promised during the [[Solaran-Khalindarian Conference of 1940]]. This made Belcanto one of the postwar states tied to the long [[Khalindarian reparations dispute]].
